Is it even possible to migrate 10 years of message history out of Slack? Users questioned whether such an export was even feasible given Slack's restrictions.
Slack's new WYSIWYG input box is terrible - users report bugs like cursor jumping past backticks, broken code formatting, and no opt-out to the old classic input box.
I've given up entirely on the Slack desktop app and use Ripcord exclusively. Much faster, more responsive and easier to use for 99% of my time spent on slack.
There is this long-standing bug on mobile versions of slack where large swaths of messages just disappear. The only way to get them back is to sign out and sign back in.
Slack developer here: at Slack we use Quip, GitHub and Jira for tracking longer-lived information rather than relying on Slack's own search/history for that purpose.

I think 'less capable moderation tools' really undersells how purposefully useless and nonexistent Slack's moderation tools are for open communities, compared to Discord which at least has some tooling.

So much information that would reduce support burdens is buried in Slacks and Discords. It can't be found through Google, and if you aren't paying for storage it all disappears after a few thousand messages.
Slack decided to close down IRC and XMPP gateways, ending third-party client access via open protocols; the IRC gateway was the only thing that made Slack usable for some users.

My biggest pain point is Slack's awful implementation of threads - you only get notified of new thread replies in a 'New Threads' view that doesn't auto-update, and you can't post snippets/files or use /me within threads.
The CUE team was looking at an $8k monthly bill for keeping Slack, prompting discussion of switching to alternatives like Zulip due to cost.

Zulip is a very good fit for open source communities, and much much better for communication than Slack. Slack encourages saying everything in the main channel; threads are close to impossible to use since they're a tiny section off to the side.

I have like 7 Slacks, 2 paid and 5 hobby ones I use once a month. Slack pushing storage/message limits on free workspaces feels like a tiny push for people to pay or leave, not a genuine resource improvement.
